subject.title: feat(skills): shared authoring standards make learned skills routable

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed automatic policy that converts correction text into generated class-level skill metadata, rather than retaining the existing topic-oriented capture behavior?
rationale: This is a product-quality choice about autonomous learning precision, routing recall, and acceptable false-positive proposals; unit assertions alone cannot establish the desired policy boundary.

options.title: Adopt after live routing proof
options.body: Accept the unified standards and generated metadata policy after a rebased branch demonstrates correct capture and selective routing on representative real sessions.

options.title: Land prompt consistency only
options.body: Keep the shared authoring standards but defer the broad deterministic correction-parser rewrite until maintainers define its precision and retention policy.

options.title: Retain current capture policy
options.body: Reject the new automatic derivation behavior if maintaining predictable topic-scoped proposal generation is more important than broader autonomous capture.

recommendation.title: Adopt after live routing proof
recommendation.body: Accept the unified standards and generated metadata policy after a rebased branch demonstrates correct capture and selective routing on representative real sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied commit series and PR rationale place this contributor closest to the proposed learning-policy behavior; current-main feature-history routing remains unconfirmed.
